definition: Risk arising from concentrated power, institutional failure, and market structure rather than from specific AI system behavior. Includes regulatory capture, monopolization, labor market disruption, and structural inequality amplified by AI deployment.
rationale_for_coinage: Skeptics locate AI risk in systemic and structural factors — power concentration, institutional capture, market dynamics — rather than in misaligned AI systems (safetyist) or regulatory overreach (accelerationist). The bare term 'risk' hides this fundamental disagreement about where danger lies.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Existential risk focuses on AI system behavior causing catastrophe; systemic risk focuses on institutional and market structure failures.
Innovation risk is about costs of over-regulation; systemic risk is about costs of under-regulation and power concentration.

contested_aspects: Whether systemic risks are more tractable than existential risks
Whether structural reform can keep pace with AI deployment
